name: Nishigahara
tagline: Otemachi in 24 minutes and Tokyo in 25 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Kita City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 24 minutes to Otemachi, 27 minutes to Shinjuku, 33 minutes to Shibuya and 39 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 23.5 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 18.7 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 23.5 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 5.1 m to 23.8 m, a difference of 18.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 4 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 17 clinics and 11 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 桑原病院, about 21 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 愛誠病院, about 34 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Namboku Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Namboku Line runs at 156% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 駒込→本駒込, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. 1LDK ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 2LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Kami-Nakazato is ahead on how close the centre is, and little else separates the two.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Nishigahara. Kami-Nakazato has the JR Keihin-Tohoku Line, a different set from Nishigahara. To Tokyo, for instance, Kami-Nakazato is 5 minutes quicker. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

neighbours.lead: Nishigahara is ahead on how close the centre is and lower rent.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Nishigahara. Sakaecho has the Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line), a different set from Nishigahara. To Toranomon, for instance, Sakaecho takes 10 minutes longer. A one-room flat costs about ¥24,000 more at Sakaecho. On safety, Nishigahara comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 9 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 7 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
